thank you mr manager good evening mr manager mr chair members of the board tonight i'd like to use two recent fires the darby house fire and the swim rva fire to give you some perspective on a part of the fire department's work that's not always readily visible when most people think about a significant fire they understandably think about the emergency response the apparatus the firefighters the evacuations the work necessary to control the incident what is less visible is what happens after the fire trucks begin to leave for significant fires the fire

marshal's office becomes one of the primary fire department resources responsible for carrying that incident forward that work can continue for days or weeks it may involve scene examinations interviews surveillance video evidence collection search warrants laboratory and forensic testing legal consultation coordination with law enforcement property owners insurance representatives and other involved parties and ultimately determining where and how the fire started in a large residential fire our role extends beyond the investigation we often remain one of the primary fire department resources assisting residents

property management as they deal with the consequences of the incident darby house and swim rva are very different fires but together they provide a good picture of the complexity importance of that work i'm going to begin with darby house this investigation remains active so there's limited information as to what i can appropriately discuss publicly but the work completed so far demonstrates why determining the cause of a significant fire can take time our personnel have returned to that property five separate times including two visits that were essentially full day operations during one of those early visits investigators recovered the

building's digital video recording system from an office that had experienced a roof collapse that video became a significant part of the investigation we were fortunate to have an intern assigned to our office who was trained to use the system he spent approximately a week and a half reviewing footage but reviewing surveillance footage as an investigation like this is not simply watching it once an interview may identify a person we did not previously know was important we may learn about a vehicle an activity or a particular time period that suddenly has

significance when that happens we have to go back watch the video again we also obtained surveillance footage from neighboring properties and worked with building management to identify individuals and vehicles captured on camera to date we've conducted 12 interviews as the investigation progressed investigators obtained a search warrant for a specific apartment recovered and processed evidence and obtained a separate court order for financial records because all of the residents have been displaced simply locating some of the individuals involved

required additional work information developed through interviews generated additional leads and several hours of follow-up at businesses in the surrounding area we've worked with henrico police personnel on forensic examination of evidence including fingerprint and dna processing later in the investigation our personnel participated in a joint exam with investigators representing multiple insurance interest by that point some material from the area of origin had already been removed during the cleanup process fortunately our investigators had extensively photographed and documented those areas beforehand during that examination we were also able to access

an area previously inaccessible because of the roof collapse that's where we were able to recover additional evidence including the resident's barbecue that they had earlier in the evening to eliminate that as a potential cause each of those steps matter an interview may change the importance of a piece of video a forensic result may support or eliminate an investigative theory access to an area that was previously inaccessible may allow us to eliminate another possible cause that is why significant fire investigations can take time at darby house we still have a couple

of additional interviews to complete before we're prepared to definitively state the cause of the fire i think that's an important point our goal is not to provide the fastest answer our responsibility is to provide the most accurate answer that can be supported by the totality of the evidence not having an immediate answer does not mean an investigation is not progressing in a complex case it often means investigators are doing the work necessary before reaching a conclusion at the same time all of the investigative work was occurring our personnel

were also dealing with the people who had suddenly lost all of their homes the building had no normal electrical service elevators were out portions of the structure had been damaged it was july it was extremely hot water mold spoiled food environmental hazards all developed quickly residents understandably wanted to get back into their apartments some needed medications or documents others were concerned about pets several primarily wanted to retrieve urns containing the

it to us that may sound like property recovery problem to that resident it was a mobility problem and it was independence those are the types of problems that continue after the emergency response ends and during those days and weeks the fire marshal's office often becomes the connection between the fire department and the people trying to recover from what happened move on to swim rva that demonstrates a different side of the same responsibility that fire occurred during the

early morning hours of july 7th 2026. unlike darby house we have completed the origin cause determination for that fire after evaluating the available evidence the fire marshal's office determined that the fire was accidental and resulted from an electrical failure or an electrical event within the building what is important for the board to understand is the amount of work necessary before we were prepared to make that determination the initial scene examination lost lasted approximately seven and a half hours during that time investigators photographed documented the building evaluated fire patterns examined the electrical system

conducted interviews reviewed surveillance footage coordinated with property owners and identified and preserved relevant evidence we also contacted chestfield fire and utilized an atf accelerant detection k9 clover during our preliminary and follow-up portions of the investigation the primary investigator returned to the property two additional occasions as the the investigation continued. In total, approximately 15 hours of the primary investigator's time was documented physically at the scene. But once again, scene time only tells a small part of the

story. A substantial amount of work took place away from the scene. One major component involved obtaining digital evidence. Investigators determined that surveillance information maintained by Ring could potentially be relevant to the investigation. Obtaining that information required researching and preparing a search warrant, presenting the warrant to a magistrate, Serving the warrant, communicating with Ring regarding the legal process, receiving the information produced in response, and then reviewing a substantial amount of digital data that was returned.

That process alone required several additional hours of investigative work that would have never appeared in CAD as time spent at the fire scene. Our personnel also spent considerable time reviewing photographs, surveillance footage, laboratory reports, electrical evidence, and investigative documents.

Evidence had to be collected, documented, and submitted to the lab. Investigators had to compare lab results with what they observed at the scene. The electrical system had to be evaluated in conjunction with the fire patterns and other physical evidence. Surveillance information had to be compared with witness statements and the developing timeline of the incident.

There was also follow-up correspondence and consultation with the Commonwealth Attorney's Office, coordination with other involved parties, the case administration, and continued review of the evidence as additional information became available. And then all that information had to be brought together in a final report.

That report was not simply a matter of writing down a conclusion. It needed to document the investigation and clearly explain how the physical evidence, the fire patterns, the electrical evidence, the laboratory findings, the surveillance information, the witness information supported that final determination.

The report went through multiple rounds of review and revision to make sure that the conclusion was clearly documented and supported by evidence. Ultimately, after completing that process, were able to definitively classify the swim rva fire as accidental and identify the electrical failure or event within the building that was the cause that conclusion is important because it demonstrates how origin and cause determinations are actually made it's not one photograph it's not one lab result it's not one witness statement or a piece of footage came from evaluating all of

those pieces of evidence together and coming to the story that they told that is what a complex origin and cause investigation requires. The visible portion of the investigation may be an investigator standing inside of a burned building, but much of the work happens afterwards.

Reviewing that evidence, analyzing photographs, obtaining records, watching videos, working with labs, evaluating electrical systems, conducting interviews, developing timelines, consulting with other professionals, and documenting why the evidence supports a particular conclusion.

For SWIM RVA, we conservatively estimate 40 hours of work by the primary investigator alone. That does not include the additional time contributed by several other members of the fire marshal's office. So while the emergency itself may have occurred during a matter of hours in July, that work was necessary to definitively determine what happened continued well beyond that morning.

So I think those two incidents demonstrate the role of the fire marshal's office better than simply listing our responsibilities. Darby House shows what an active, complex investigation looks like when there is still work to be completed before we are prepared to definitively state what caused the fire.

SWIM RVA shows what the process looks like when it reaches completion. An investigation involving extensive scene examination, physical, intellectual evidence, laboratory testing, surveillance, and digital evidence, legal process, and many hours of follow-up that ultimately allowed us to reach a definitive conclusion.

They also demonstrate why significant fire investigation sometimes takes weeks and months to complete. Our responsibility is not to provide the quickest answer. Our responsibility is to provide an answer that is accurate, objective, and supported by evidence.

And throughout that process, the Fire Marshal's Office provides continuity for the fire department. Someone has to preserve and evaluate the evidence. Someone has to conduct the interviews and review the hours of video. Someone has to work with the laboratories, law enforcement partners, property owners, insurance representatives, attorneys, and other involved parties.

Someone has to continue helping residents after a major residential fire when they're trying to recover medications, pets, mobility equipment, and irreplaceable belongings. And ultimately, someone has to put all that information together to determine what happened.

For our fire department, that responsibility belongs to the fire marshal's office. emergency response may last hours our involvement may continue for days weeks or months in many ways the fire marshal's office is a part of the fire department that remains after the fire trucks have left continuing the investigation assisting those affected coordinating with our partners and carrying the incident through to its conclusion darby house and swim rva are two very good examples
